note_on_versions: All six sources are living web documents, not release-pinned artifacts; identity recorded as site+path at capture time. MQTT v5.0 is a dated OASIS standard (os edition).

sources.identity: MQTT Version 5.0, OASIS Standard, 07 March 2019 (os edition)
sources.mechanism_family: messaging-protocol delivery semantics (IoT/pub-sub analogy, not a survey competitor)
locators: Section 4.3 Quality of Service levels and protocol flows (QoS 0/1/2, at-least-once vs exactly-once handshakes)
Section 3.3.1 DUP flag (server MUST set DUP=1 on redelivery; 'DUP flag set to 0' on first send)
Section 3.3.2.3 Message Expiry Interval (broker-side retention/TTL of undelivered messages)
sources.used_for: ack meaning per QoS level; duplicates are normal under retry; retry resumption after reconnect; message expiry analogy

sources.identity: AWS Builders' Library article 'Timeouts, retries, and backoff with jitter' (Marc Brooker, AWS; living web page)
locators: Sections on backoff with jitter and retry budgets; full-page search 'jitter', 'retry budget'
sources.used_for: bounded exponential backoff + jitter; retry budget idea; retry storm risk

sources.identity: Stripe API Reference, 'Idempotent requests' (living web doc, React shell with embedded doc text)
locators: Header 'Idempotency-Key'; text nodes containing 'Idempotency-Key'/'idempoten*' in embedded doc data
sources.used_for: client-generated stable key so replay of an unacknowledged request is safe; key tied to request payload

sources.identity: PouchDB guide 'Conflicts' (living web doc; PouchDB = CouchDB replication client used offline-first on phones)
sources.mechanism_family: offline-first local persistence + sync with revision/tree conflict handling (database replication analogy)
locators: Guide sections on conflicts, deterministic winner, merging/leader election
sources.used_for: alternative to retry-until-ack: persistent local store + deterministic merge; conflicts instead of dedup

sources.identity: SQLite documentation 'Atomic Commit In SQLite' (version-of-record is the live sqlite.org page; stable doc)
sources.mechanism_family: durable local persistence under power loss (embedded database)
locators: Sections: transaction boundary, hardware/OS/power failure assumptions, journal/WAL commit sequence
sources.used_for: queue durability on phones: commit ordering vs fsync; item must survive crash before any ack of local enqueue

sources.identity: microservices.io 'Pattern: Transactional outbox' (Chris Richardson; living web page)
locators: Pattern sections: Problem, Forces, Solution, 'idempotent' consumer note
sources.used_for: making the local queue itself transactional with state; relay + consumer idempotency
